title: Clockfall ledger repair for interleaved quota windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background repair job and API-level controls for tenant quota ledgers that became interleaved across multiple reset boundaries due to clock drift, DST boundary changes, and partial failovers. The goal is to provide an idempotent, observable ledger-repair process that restores correct usage windows, preserves reserved-capacity guarantees, and avoids double-counting or lost credits.
background: We observed several customer incidents where quota windows for reserved pools overlapped after a cross-region cutover plus an NTP-induced clock shift. The accounting ledger accepted writes to both pre-cutover and post-cutover windows, producing interleaved usage rows and causing incorrect remaining quota calculations. Existing reconciliation tools assume monotonic epoch ranges and cannot safely backfill or compact overlapping ranges without risking invoice drift or user-visible throttling anomalies.
design_notes: Introduce a repair worker that operates on per-tenant ledgers and performs three phases: detect interleaving, compute a canonical boundary mapping, and apply a rewrite that preserves monotonic cumulative counters.
Use time-bucket watermarking: prefer the tenant-configured billing anchor when available, otherwise derive boundary from last successful checkpoint and highest contiguous sequence number.
Make all ledger writes idempotent via deterministic operation keys and a two-phase commit pattern that writes a tombstone + replacement rows; finalization uses compare-and-swap on ledger epoch IDs.
Limit the repair scope to tenants flagged for 'repair-needed' to avoid large global migrations and provide a dry-run mode that emits proposed deltas to a newline-delimited JSON S3 path for review.
Expose 'repair preview' endpoints in the admin console and include per-tenant risk score based on overlap size and reserved-capacity exposure.
Ensure cross-region repairs coordinate via leader election to avoid concurrent conflicting rewrites; use existing coordinator service for leasing.
Preserve original raw rows for 90 days in immutable storage for audit and potential rollback; redact PII before storing preview outputs.
This approach avoids rolling global resets and minimizes customer-impact by pacing repairs and keeping live quota enforcement consistent with last-accepted checkpoint until rewrite finalizes.
Metric hooks: emit pre/post corrections and delta counts; integrate with billing reconciliation pipeline to surface any invoice-impacting adjustments.
Security: require security_review_required flag and audit log entries for any repair finalization action.
UX: add an admin table with suggested repairs, estimated time, and 'approve/apply' action per tenant.
Fallbacks: if repair fails midway, system should revert to tombstone state and unblock live writes to a safe fallback epoch to preserve availability.
We will not attempt automated monetary refunds in this ticket; adjustments will be surfaced to finance for manual review after repair completion.
Rollout will start with a small set of internal test tenants in dedicated capacity, then pilot with a single low-risk customer before broadening.
Coordinate with billing and legal for tenants with enterprise contracts before any ledger rewrite that could alter invoiced usage.
Performance considerations: repair worker must throttle writes to avoid GC pressure and to respect tenant rate limits; leverage batched apply and kernel-friendly payload sizes.
Compatibility: ensure repaired ledgers remain compatible with runtime quota lookups and the rate limiter's reservoir model.
Add a chronic job that detects new interleavings and alerts on trend increases to prevent recurrence.
We will add acceptance tests that simulate clock drift, leader flaps, and DST transitions to validate the repair path.
Document expected audit artifacts and the rollback procedure in Confluence and link to the PR for the repair worker implementation.
Estimate assumes 3 backend engineers for two sprints plus one half-time SRE for rollout support.

Implement detect-and-preview endpoint that returns proposed delta and risk score (owner: Marcus)
Build repair-worker prototype with idempotent apply and two-phase commit (owner: Backend Team)
Add admin console UI for preview/approve/apply actions (owner: Console UX)
Integrate metrics and tracer spans into repair flow (owner: SRE)
Create dry-run storage path and retention policy (owner: Storage)
End-to-end tests simulating NTP skew and cross-region cutover (owner: QA)
Pilot run on internal reserved tenants and capture telemetry (owner: Oncall)
Finance/legal sync and approval before customer pilot (owner: PM)
Post-mortem and runbook updates based on pilot results (owner: Incident Lead)
acceptance_criteria: Repair worker can detect interleaved quota windows and generate a human-readable preview showing before/after ledger rows
Idempotent apply succeeds and final ledger passes invariants: monotonic cumulative usage, no double-counting, and total usage preserved for non-overlapping windows
Admin console preview and apply actions are implemented and gated by RBAC and audit logging
Pilot executed on at least 3 internal tenants with metrics showing no customer-visible throttling regressions
Integration tests for clock drift and DST boundary transitions pass in CI
Monitoring dashboards show pre/post correction deltas and an alert triggers for unexpected magnitude of corrections
Finance confirms no automated invoice drift; manual adjustments surfaced where necessary and documented
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only run against synthetic and internal reserved tenants (1 week)
Beta: limited customer pilot with explicit customer consent and legal signoff (2 weeks)
Ramp: expand to low-risk customers with monitoring and SRE on-call (4 weeks)
GA: open repair self-service in admin console with guardrails and opt-in policies (post-approval)
monitoring_and_metrics: alert if delta_rows_total > 1% of tenant_monthly_tokens or repair.duration_ms > 1 hour
risks: Misapplied repairs could change invoiced usage; mitigate by preview + finance signoff
Concurrent repairs from different regions could conflict; mitigate with leader election and lease coordination
Large tenants may require long-running repairs that need to be throttled to avoid degradation
Edge cases for very sparse ledger retention may lack sufficient anchors for canonicalization; fallback to manual review
Legal/enterprise customers may refuse automated ledger changes; provide manual remediation support
